state.label: El Niño Advisory · Historic Event Likely
state.detail: El Niño continued to intensify through the autumn, with eastern-Pacific SST anomalies near +4°C. CPC (Oct 8) now puts an 83% chance of a historic event (≥+2.5°C on 3-month RONI) during Oct–Dec — up from 75% in September — which would exceed any El Niño since 1950. The multimodel peak is near +3.5°C.

narrative: El Niño has intensified to the brink of a historic event. Per the CPC's October 8 discussion, the September monthly Niño indices reached +2.1°C (Niño-3.4), +3.0°C (Niño-3) and +3.9°C (Niño-1+2), and the weekly Niño 3.4 centred on October 14 climbed to +3.3°C, with the IRI multimodel average projecting a peak near +3.5°C in OND–NDJ. The subsurface remains well above average with a deeper-than-average thermocline. CPC now carries an 83% chance of a historic event exceeding +2.5°C on the 3-month RONI during Oct–Dec — up from 75% in September and 69% in August — which would surpass every El Niño since 1950. IRI's mid-October plume is unanimous: all 27 models forecast very strong from OND through DJF, with about 10 reaching or exceeding +3.5°C, and El Niño probability is 100% from OND 2026 through MAM 2027. The positive IOD that co-developed (DMI +0.51°C in September, forecast positive through December) softened the monsoon's back half, but the Indian season still closed ~13% below normal — its worst since 2015. The only open question now is the magnitude of the record.
